verdict.headline: Toyota Corolla Cross Hybrid
verdict.text: Best risk-adjusted package: lowest modeled five-year cost of any SUV here, a mature non-turbo hybrid, and the strongest likely residual. The Sportage is the better buy when physical space matters more; the Niro maximises efficiency per shekel.

criteria.label: 5-yr cost
criteria.hint: Depreciation + fees + insurance + energy + maintenance. Excludes purchase price itself (that would double-count) and financing interest.

criteria.label: Cash price
criteria.hint: MSRP plus first-registration fee — the cash needed to acquire the car.

criteria.label: Reliability
criteria.hint: Analyst outlook 1-10 based on powertrain maturity and local track record. Not an owner-survey score — Israeli owner data is fragmented.

criteria.label: Safety
criteria.hint: Analyst score 1-10 weighting Euro NCAP result AND test-protocol recency. An old 5-star is not a new 5-star.

criteria.label: Consumption
criteria.hint: Official or locally quoted L/100 km. Undefined for the PHEV, where consumption depends entirely on charging habit.

criteria.label: Cargo
criteria.hint: Boot volume with all fitted seats in use. For three-row cars this is the all-rows-up figure — see the folded figure in the detail view.

criteria.label: 5-yr energy
criteria.hint: Petrol and/or electricity over five years, recomputed live from your assumptions.

criteria.label: 5-yr residual
criteria.hint: Modeled share of list price retained after five years. This is the single largest uncertainty in the whole comparison.

criteria.label: Seats
criteria.hint: Set this to 0 unless you actually carry more than five people.

criteria.label: Power
criteria.hint: Combined system output where the importer publishes it.

limitations: Dealer discounts are opaque. There is no authoritative database of actual Israeli transaction prices by trim; the negotiation bands here are targets inferred from current campaign behaviour, not promises.

Israeli owner-review data is fragmented and not statistically representative, especially for 2026 newcomers like the Symbioz and Tucson PHEV. Reliability scores are analyst outlooks, not survey results.
Warranty and scheduled-maintenance detail is inconsistently published. Obtain the exact 2026 warranty booklet and service schedule in writing before paying a non-refundable deposit.

Future depreciation dominates TCO uncertainty. Fuel cost can be calculated; nobody knows what a 2026 hybrid sells for in 2031. Use these numbers to separate broad economic tiers, not to the last ₪1,000.
Published MSRP is not the transaction price. Importers use campaigns, display-car offers, finance subsidies and trade-in boosts instead of openly cutting list prices.
Financing interest is excluded. Illustratively, ₪150,000 over 60 months at a hypothetical 7% nominal rate generates roughly ₪28,000 of interest — enough to erase any discount you negotiate.

steps: Verify official Israeli MSRP and exact drivetrain
Obtain insurance quotes before choosing the model
Drive with a normal family load
Check child seats, stroller, parking and highway noise
Request a written cash quotation
Negotiate trade-in separately
Compare bank, importer and external finance on total shekels repaid
Confirm warranty and maintenance schedule in writing
Review VIN, model year and delivery terms
Pay a deposit only against a written order
Confirm cancellation and delay provisions
Arrange compulsory and comprehensive insurance
Install the home charger if buying the PHEV
Dealer processes first registration
Inspect paint, wheels, glass and accessories
Record odometer and VIN
Verify two keys, manuals, warranty and charging cable
Follow service-book intervals
Renew registration and insurance annually
Keep invoices and hybrid/PHEV battery checks for resale
